title: S3/G3: Geometric fixed points of O-slice cells and closure under the filtration

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Necessity direction, computational core.** To prove that membership in $\tau^{\aO}_{\ge n}$ implies the geometric-fixed-point connectivity bound, compute $\Phi^H$ on the generators and show the bound is preserved.

**To prove.**
1. Double-coset/Weyl formula for geometric fixed points of an induction: $\Phi^H(G_+\wedge_K Y)\simeq \bigvee_{[g]\in (H\backslash G/K)_{\mathrm{rel}}}\Phi^{H\cap{}^gK}(c_g^* Y)$, with the correct index set.
2. $\Phi^K S^{m\rho_K}\simeq S^{m}$, more generally $\Phi^K S^{V}\simeq S^{\dim V^K}$.
3. Deduce the connectivity of $\Phi^H(G_+\wedge_K S^{m\rho_K})$ and verify it equals the claimed $f_{\aO}(n,H)$ bound on generators.
4. Show the connectivity bound is closed under the colimits and extensions defining $\tau^{\aO}_{\ge n}$, using exactness/colimit-preservation of $\Phi^H$ and closure of connectivity in $\mathrm{Sp}$.

Reference: HHR 2016 §B (geometric fixed points), Hill primer.

comments.author: solver-agent
comments.body:
**Resolution of q5-29 (necessity direction: geometric fixed points of O-slice cells and closure under the filtration).**

I reviewed the existing proof and found that the computational core requested by this issue was, in substance, already present and rigorous, distributed across:

- **Prop. `prop:phiNT`** ($\Phi^G N^T S^1 \simeq S^{|T/G|}$, fully proved via $N^TS^1\cong S^{\mathbb R\cdot T}$ and $\Phi^G S^V\simeq S^{V^G}$);
- **Lemma `lem:index`** (the index bound $|T|\le r_H\cdot|T/H|$, $r_H=[H:\chi^{\mathcal O}(H)]$);
- **Lemma `lem:restr`** (the full Mackey double-coset formula for $i_H^*$ of an induction, used to reduce to the top group);
- **Lemma `lem:forward`** (Steps 0-4: per-subgroup reduction; $\Phi^G$ kills proper inductions; closure of the $\Phi^G$-connectivity bound under (o1)-(o3); generators satisfy the bound).

To make the proof transparently complete against the four explicit items, I added two passages.

**1. General geometric-fixed-point double-coset (Weyl) formula** (new `eq:phi-dc`, Step 1' of `lem:forward`):
$$\Phi^H(G_+\wedge_K Y)\simeq\bigvee_{[g]\in H\backslash G/K:\,H\subseteq gKg^{-1}}\Phi^H(c_g\,i^*_{g^{-1}Hg}Y),$$
derived from the Mackey formula + $\Phi^H\simeq\Phi^H i_H^*$ + the proper-induction vanishing. I explain that necessity only needs the top-group special case (empty wedge, hence $\Phi^G(G_+\wedge_K Y)\simeq0$ for $K\subsetneq G$), because Step 0 already moved evaluation to the top group of $(H,\mathcal O|_H)$. This addresses **item 1** and clarifies why the slick vanishing in Step 1 suffices.

**2. Regular-representation slice cells** (new `rem:rho-cells`): $\rho_K=\mathbb R\cdot(K/e)$, so $S^{m\rho_K}\cong N^{\coprod_1^m K/e}S^1$, and Prop. `prop:phiNT` (equivalently `eq:phiSV` with $(m\rho_K)^K\cong\mathbb R^m$) gives $\Phi^K S^{m\rho_K}\simeq S^m$. This addresses **item 2** in classical HHR form, noting that in the incomplete setting $K/e$ need not be admissible -- the reason the proof works with general admissible-norm cells $N^TS^1$.

**Items 3 and 4** were already complete: Step 3 of `lem:forward` deduces $\mathrm{conn}(\Phi^G N^TS^1)=|T/G|$ and verifies $r_G\cdot|T/G|\ge|T|\ge n$ on generators (matching the bound $n/r_H$); Step 2 verifies closure under colimits, cofibers-of-objects, extensions, retracts, and orbit tensors via exactness/colimit-preservation of $\Phi^G$ and one-sided closure of $\mathrm{Sp}_{\ge m}$. I sanity-checked $|T|\le r_H|T/H|$ on $C_4$ examples (complete and trivial transfer systems); consistent.

No mathematical gap remained; the edits make all four requested steps explicit and self-contained. (LaTeX toolchain not installed, so no compile; I verified $-balance, macro hygiene, and that all referenced labels resolve.)

Marking resolved.
